basics.name: Fahridana Ahmad Rayyansyah
basics.summary: Backend engineer who measures before optimising. Builds Go and Laravel services on PostgreSQL and Redis, then load-tests them with k6 to find where the time actually goes. A 336-run benchmark of four cache strategies showed the cache was not the bottleneck.

points: Rewrote the Performance Appraisal system from native PHP to Laravel 12 on MySQL for 200+ employees.
Replaced a manual 2 to 3 day quarterly entry step with an HRIS sync and bulk Excel import, saving 8 to 12 working days a year.
Added periods with deadlines and locking, dashboards and Excel/PDF export, then trained the admins who run it.
Built a video summarisation pipeline: the service follows a YouTube channel by ID, reads each new video's auto-captions, and calls the OpenAI API for a summary and keywords.
Shipped the interface in Next.js and TypeScript, and documented shared Radix components in Storybook with Jest tests.

projects.name: muara
points: Built muara, a Python 3.14 tool that pulls JobStreet, Greenhouse and Kalibrr into one local database, records which of four facts a run ended in, and settles which jobs have closed.

projects.name: meiro, open source
points: Merged three pull requests into meiro, a 30-star Go YouTube Music client: a Flatpak Discord socket path, every artist in rich presence, and Firefox and Zen sign-in.
Traced why rich presence retried forever on Flatpak Discord, and covered the new artist field with Go tests.

projects.name: LMS Cache Strategy Benchmark
points: Built a Moodle-style LMS in Laravel 12 to test four cache strategies behind one interface, switched by one env value.
Modelled role inheritance and per-user conditional availability, so cache keys follow the access model instead of a shared key.
Ran 336 k6 runs over 112 combinations of cache strategy, workload, Redis topology and concurrency up to 2,000 users, then tested the results with ANOVA and Tukey HSD instead of reading charts by eye.

No strategy beat another: throughput stayed between 53 and 72 req/s across every valid run, and CPU held at 86% or above from 100 users. The bottleneck was Eloquent hydration and repeated context resolution, not the data source.

projects.name: Pendekinlink, URL Shortener
points: Built a Hono shortener where Redis absorbs click counters, so a hot link does not serialise on a PostgreSQL row lock.
Put rate limiting in Redis-backed middleware, kept the schema in one Drizzle package, and deployed the monorepo to a VPS.

projects.name: HRIS, Human Resource Information System
points: Built the seat-based subscription path on a Go (Gin, GORM) backend: the server owns the Midtrans charge and webhook, so a seat count moves only after the provider confirms payment.
Built geofenced attendance with live maps in Next.js, containerised the stack with Docker, and deployed to Azure.
